report_name: BlackX: New UEFI Bootkit with BlackLotus Similarities Emerges

threat_actors.name: Unknown APT Group targeting Central Asia
threat_actors.description: An unknown, highly motivated, and well-resourced Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) group, likely a nation-state actor, responsible for deploying the BlackX UEFI bootkit in a targeted campaign against diplomatic organizations in Central Asia for long-term espionage and intelligence gathering.

attack_patterns.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Bootkit
attack_patterns.description: BlackX is a UEFI bootkit that embeds itself within the system's firmware to achieve persistence, executing before the operating system loads.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: The kernel driver loaded by the BlackX bootkit is used to disable endpoint security products and other security features like PatchGuard.

attack_patterns.name: Rootkit
attack_patterns.description: BlackX functions as a rootkit to hide its presence and the presence of other malware on the compromised system, making it invisible to most security software.

attack_patterns.name: Kernel Modules and Extensions
attack_patterns.description: The BlackX bootkit loads its own malicious, unsigned driver into the Windows kernel to gain kernel-level privileges and inject malware into legitimate processes.

malware.name: BlackX
malware.description: A highly sophisticated UEFI bootkit used in targeted attacks against diplomatic agencies. It is capable of bypassing Secure Boot to establish persistent and stealthy control over a system by loading a malicious kernel driver.

malware.name: BlackLotus
malware.description: A notorious UEFI bootkit mentioned for its similarities in design and capabilities to the BlackX bootkit, suggesting the threat actors behind BlackX may have access to its source code or are building upon similar techniques.

tools.name: bcdedit.exe
tools.description: The bcdedit.exe utility may be used by attackers to modify boot configuration data as part of the bootkit deployment process.

vulnerabilities.name: Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.description: A known but unspecified vulnerability is exploited by the attackers to add their own malicious bootloader to the list of trusted executables, subverting the Secure Boot process.

identities.name: Diplomatic organizations
identities.description: Diplomatic agencies in Central Asia were the targets of the campaign deploying the BlackX bootkit.

indicators.name: BlackX Secure Boot State Registry Key
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: BlackX Secure Boot State Registry Monitoring
id: 2a9b3c1d-e8f7-4a6b-9c1d-e8f7a6b9c1d2
status: experimental
description: Monitors for modifications to the SecureBoot state registry key, which could indicate tampering by a bootkit like BlackX.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-24
tags:
  - attack.t1542.003
  - attack.t1014
level: high
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains: '\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecureBoot\State'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects access or modification of the Windows registry key that stores the state of Secure Boot. This was mentioned as a hunting hint for detecting BlackX activity.

indicators.name: Suspicious BCDEDIT Execution for Bootkit Deployment
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious BCDEDIT Execution for Bootkit Deployment
id: 3b8c2d1e-f9a8-4b7c-8d2e-f9a8b7c8d2e3
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of bcdedit.exe, which attackers may use to modify boot configuration data when deploying a bootkit like BlackX.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-24
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity, system updates, or dual-boot configuration changes.
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1542.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of bcdedit.exe, which is a hunting hint for the potential deployment of the BlackX bootkit.

indicators.name: Suspicious EFI File Creation on ESP
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious EFI File Creation on ESP
id: 4c7d3e2f-a0b9-4c8d-9e3f-a0b9c8d9e3f4
status: experimental
description: 'Monitors for the creation of new or unrecognized .efi files on the EFI System Partition (ESP), a technique used by bootkits like BlackX to establish persistence.'
references:
  - https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-24
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate firmware updates or bootloader installations.
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1542.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.efi'
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - 'C:\EFI\'
      - 'C:\Windows\Boot\EFI\'
      - '\\?\Volume{'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects the creation of new .efi files on the EFI System Partition, which is a key behavior of bootkits like BlackX for achieving persistence.
